$comment: Ambient lighting (docs/DAY_NIGHT.md §10, ARCHITECTURE.md §6.1): what darkens the hemisphere (sky) light on terrain, baked into each vertex at mesh time; the direct sun and moon are not touched. ao: classic voxel corner occlusion; each of its three levels below open darkens the ambient by strength / 3 (strength 1: a corner tucked into a full crease gets none). sky: the baked sky visibility, the share of `rays` short rays that escape. Each ray leaves the vertex in a cosine-weighted hemisphere about the face's normal turned toward the face's sky (a ray below the face-local horizon is mirrored above it) and runs `lengthM` metres through the voxel grid; one that gets that far is then probed `probeM` metres straight up (face-local) from its end and counts as blocked if anything solid is over it (a cave roof, an overhang beyond the ray's reach). The reach (lengthM across, lengthM + probeM up) must stay inside the meshers' apron (dwell_world::SKY_APRON; dwell-look checks it at build time). rays 0 turns the sky visibility off. floor: the share of the ambient a fully occluded vertex keeps (ambient = hemisphere × (floor + (1 − floor) × ao × visibility)). Every entry changes the meshes: run `node shared/look/ambient.mjs` after editing; CI fails if crates/dwell-look/src/ambient.gen.rs is stale.
